title: Finding Disposition
description:
An AUTHORIZED decision that a specific finding should not block.

THE INVARIANT: a disposition does not mutate evidence. It changes ENFORCEMENT against that evidence. The original observation is preserved forever. Without this rule the exception layer becomes destructive deduplication wearing governance perfume.

THE HARDENING: dispositions are consumed from the PROTECTED DEFAULT BRANCH, never from the PR under evaluation. Otherwise a PR can exempt the secret it introduces in the same PR -- 'secrets always block unless I add myself to the exemption file' is not a control.

fingerprint.description: Stable identity of THIS finding. Exact match only -- never a rule-wide or path-wide mute, which takes the next real occurrence with it.

scope_path.description: Narrowest path that resolves it. A broad allowlist is cheap today and an invisibility cloak forever.

disposition_type.description: Four MATERIALLY DIFFERENT truth claims. Collapsing them produces 'remediated' findings a scanner detects forever.

compensating_control.description: REQUIRED when disposition_type is MITIGATED. Naming the control is what distinguishes mitigation from acceptance.

approver_role.description: A ROLE, never a person -- nothing orphans at handoff. Proposing is not approving.

expires.description: Expiry is the mechanism. Silence must NEVER renew a disposition. THE WINDOW DIFFERS BY TYPE -- see expiry_policy: a remediation claim and a risk acceptance are not the same kind of promise and must not carry the same lifetime.

state.$comment: Only 'approved' suppresses. A proposal never buys passage.

then.$comment: Accepting a real risk requires a record of who accepted it and under what conditions.

expiry_policy.$comment: Non-standard key, deliberate: this is contract guidance the validator cannot express, and burying it in prose is how it gets lost.

REMEDIATED.rule: SHORT-LIVED BY DESIGN. This is not a suppression record -- it is a claim that the condition is gone. It must be revalidated by the next scan.
REMEDIATED.self_invalidating: If the scanner still reproduces the finding, the remediation claim FAILED or went stale. It must stop suppressing immediately, not at expiry. This is the only disposition a scanner can falsify by itself.

MITIGATED.rule: A compensating control can legitimately persist, but it must be REVALIDATED -- controls decay, get reconfigured, or get removed by someone who did not know why they existed.

ACCEPTED_RISK.rule: A real risk knowingly carried. The expiry is what forces a fresh, dated decision instead of a permanent one made once by someone who has since left.

FALSE_POSITIVE.rule: Longest-lived, because the detector being wrong is a stable fact.
FALSE_POSITIVE.invalidate_when: The fingerprint, rule or path changes MATERIALLY. A detector that was wrong about one thing is not thereby wrong about a different thing at the same path.
